picks.thesis: AAPL demonstrates consistent quality growth with strong free cash flow and a dominant ecosystem. Recent pullback to 50-day moving average presents an attractive entry point. Valuation remains reasonable with a forward P/E of ~28x, below its 5-year average. Upcoming iPhone 16 cycle and AI integration into services should drive revenue growth.

Mastercard exhibits high-quality growth characteristics with a wide moat in global payments. Recent earnings beat highlights resilience in cross-border volumes. Valuation is reasonable at ~32x forward earnings, supported by 15%+ revenue growth. Technicals show a bull flag pattern forming, suggesting continuation of the uptrend.

UnitedHealth Group represents quality growth in healthcare with diversified revenue streams. Medicare Advantage growth remains robust, and Optum segment continues to outperform. Valuation is attractive at ~20x forward earnings with consistent 12-15% EPS growth. Recent pullback to 200-day moving average offers a favorable risk-reward entry.

Walmart's valuation appears stretched at ~25x forward earnings despite modest growth expectations. Recent strength driven by inflationary pressures rather than true growth. Technicals show overbought conditions with RSI >70 and price at upper Bollinger Band. Quality growth investors should avoid this low-margin, low-growth retailer at current levels.
UNI forming a bullish falling wedge on the 4h chart, with RSI divergence suggesting weakening downtrend momentum. Breakout above $7.30 with volume confirmation could target $8.50+.

INJ rejected at key resistance ($25.50) with bearish engulfing candle on daily timeframe. 4h chart shows overbought RSI and descending volume profile, suggesting potential pullback to $21 support zone.

APT consolidating above 200-day MA with bullish MACD crossover on 4h chart. Recent retest of $7.50 support with decreasing selling volume suggests accumulation phase. Breakout above $8.00 could target $9.50+.

FFIE trending on Reddit/WallStreetBets with increasing mentions and call option volume. Price consolidating near 52-week lows with short interest > 30%, setting up for a potential short squeeze. Retail momentum building as EV narrative gains traction.

SOXS exhibiting retail overcrowding with excessive call buying and low float. Semiconductor sector showing signs of exhaustion (e.g., NVDA, SMH pullback), and SOXS inversely correlated. Dealers long gamma, suggesting downward delta hedging flow likely. High short interest (>40%) but price near resistance with bearish divergence on RSI.
